minutes.headline: Sewer Commission approved policy updates, set a budget workshop and a public hearing, and heard pump capacity concerns.
minutes.summary: The commission heard the contract operator on station maintenance and pump capacity, with concern about a possible 40B development. It voted by roll call to approve sewer policy updates, which go to a public hearing, and scheduled a budget workshop. It also approved two sets of prior minutes, reviewed grease trap non-compliance, and agreed to keep a Valentine's Day meeting.

what_happened.line: The Sewer Commission voted by roll call, with no dissent, to approve sewer policy updates, including a laterals change from counsel, and send them to a public hearing.
The public hearing on the policy changes is set for the start of the 28th meeting, with 10 days' posting and no town meeting vote needed.
A budget workshop was set for the 7th at 7 PM, to be posted as a meeting with the budget as its only item.
The contract operator reported on station maintenance and pump capacity, with concern raised about a possible 40B development.
A restaurant was told to have its grease trap pumped by February 18, and a non-responding establishment faces a fine that grows each day.

why_it_matters: The sewer policy changes, including how laterals are handled, take effect only after the public hearing, which is where a resident can comment before the rules are set.
Pump capacity concerns tied to a possible 40B development bear on whether the sewer system can serve new housing without added cost to ratepayers.
The commission is an enterprise fund, paid for by sewer bills rather than general taxes, so its budget workshop and the March finance committee presentation set what sewer users are charged.
